chunk_id: Business Plan Guidance, 1. Introduction - 4d168879faad357a
body:
An applicant is required to submit a business plan to the Authority, alongside a completed application form.
Firms are required to operate in accordance with a business plan and to update its business plan following any material changes, providing a copy to the Authority.  Where submitting an update to the business plan, the firm must provide the Authority with details of any changes to the information required to be submitted by an applicant as part of an application.
This guidance summarises the content for a typical business plan for an application or update due to a material change. A business plan should not be provided in summary form using bullet points, instead it must provide full details together with an explanation of the information included in it.
It is appreciated that:

1. The extent and detail of a business plan will vary according to the nature, scale and complexity of the business or proposed business.

2. Applicants/firms which are branches will operate in accordance with a business plan set by their head office and, similarly, subsidiaries of international organisations may operate within a corporate style.

3. Applicants/firms which are locally incorporated banks will cover many relevant aspects in their Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process.

chunk_id: Business Plan Guidance, 1. Introduction - a37fb6743f383280
body:
This guidance also sets out the related documents which may be needed to support the information included within a business plan. If supporting documentation is provided as part of the application, it should be clearly referenced back to the relevant section of the guidance using the relevant checklist in 3. Supporting Documentation.
Some sections of this guidance apply to all applicants, whilst some are only relevant to specific types of applicant. Specific provisions for certain types of FSA08 and IA08 applicants can be found in Appendix 2: Financial Services Act 2008 - Additional Provisions, and in Appendix 3:  Insurance Act 2008 - Additional Provisions.
During the processing of the application or submission of an updated business plan, the Authority may ask the applicant/firm to provide information over and above that which is included in its business plan.
The content of a business plan, as summarised in this document, is not intended to be comprehensive nor is it intended to be a template. An applicant/firm is encouraged to consider what is likely to be relevant to the Authority's assessment of its application/business plan update, taking into account the nature of the applicant's activities or proposed activities.

chunk_id: Business Plan Guidance, 2. Requirements for Applicants, 2.1 Background/Objectives, All applicants: - 3db12cc20517ae2a

- A summary of the rationale for the applicant seeking an authorisation and establishing in the Isle of Man, together with the business objectives and strategy. For start-ups, the rationale for entering the chosen business area.

- i) The full legal ownership of the applicant, including the name, place of incorporation and the relevant percentage holdings and voting rights of any parent companies (direct or indirect);
- ii) All controllers of the applicant (as defined in Section 48 of the FSA08 or in Section 54 of the IA08) including the relevant percentage holdings and voting rights, and Controlled Function references;
- iii) The beneficial ownership of the applicant, where this is different to (i) and (ii) above;

chunk_id: Business Plan Guidance, Appendix 1: Example Financial Summary Tables, (iii) IA08 non long-term applicant forecast financial information - f8527542912124bb
headers: (iii) IA08 non long-term applicant forecast financial information
body:
[Editors note: the below is a flattened table]
Presented for each year of the 3-year forecast period:
- Income statement: premiums written, reinsurance premium written, change in unearned premium reserve (UPR) and reinsurance UPR, giving net premium earned; claims paid, movements in claims reserves, unexpired risk reserve (URR) and incurred but not reported (IBNR) reserve, reinsurance recovered and movement in reinsurance recoverable, giving net claims; reinsurance broking fees and change in deferred broking fees; underwriting profit/(loss); investment income; expenses; profit/(loss) for the period; dividends.
- Balance sheet: assets (bank balances and cash, intercompany loan, unearned reinsurance premium reserve, deferred reinsurance broking costs, recoverable from reinsurers, prepaid expenses, total assets); general business insurance provisions (UPR, claims reserves, URR); other liabilities (accrued expenses); net assets; represented by share capital, share premium and retained earnings, giving total shareholder's funds.
- Solvency Capital Requirement (SCR): absolute own funds, SCR figure, shareholder's funds, solvency surplus/(deficit) and solvency ratio.

body:

Presented for each year of the 5-year forecast period:
- Revenue account: written premiums, fee income, investment income, realised and unrealised gains/(losses) on linked and non-linked assets and other income, giving total income (A); surrenders and partial surrenders and other claims, giving total claims (B); acquisition and renewal expenses (including commission), investment management expenses, one-off expenses, other expenses and taxation, giving total expenses (C); net assets brought forward, excess of income over expenditure (A)+(B)+(C), capital injected, dividends paid or payable, and net assets carried forward.
- Solvency: SCR, eligible capital resources and SCR ratio; Minimum Capital Requirement (MCR), eligible capital resources and MCR ratio.
